title: Immune Responses and Protective Efficacy of a Recombinant GCSF‐Adjuvanted Formalin‐Killed Streptococcus parauberis Vaccine in Starry Flounder (Platichthys stellatus)
content:
ABSTRACT

Streptococcus parauberis is an important bacterial pathogen of cultured marine fish. This study evaluated recombinant granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (rGCSF) as an immunostimulant and molecular adjuvant for a formalin-killed S. parauberis vaccine in starry flounder (Platichthys stellatus). Fish received rGCSF at 10, 50 or 100 μg/mL, and kidney expression of immune-related genes was assessed by quantitative real-time PCR. rGCSF induced gene- and time-dependent changes in IL-1β, IL-8, CD11b, BCL2 and MyD88, with MyD88 increasing approximately 450-fold in the 100 μg/mL group. For vaccination, fish received 1 mg formalin-killed cells (FKC)/fish alone or with rGCSF at 50, 100 or 150 μg/mL and were challenged 6 weeks later. FKC alone induced antigen-specific serum antibody responses but provided incomplete protection. In contrast, the FKC + rGCSF 150 μg/mL group showed 100% survival during the 21-day challenge. Protection was not monotonic across rGCSF concentrations, and serum antibody magnitude did not directly correspond with survival. These findings support further evaluation of rGCSF as a molecular adjuvant for S. parauberis vaccination in starry flounder.
